meta.scope: Lower body, hinge, core and power exercises for Forge procedural skeleton animation (FK + 2-bone IK).

conventions.trunkFromVertical: forward lean of the pelvis-to-neck line from gravity vertical, positive forward; null for supine/prone/seated where bodyPlane is given instead (optional trunkFromHorizontal: positive = head end higher than hips)
conventions.hipFlexion: thigh flexion relative to trunk (negative = extension). When spineFlexion is present, hipFlexion is thigh relative to pelvis.
conventions.ankleDorsiflexion: shin forward of perpendicular to the foot; negative = plantarflexion. For machines it is relative to the footplate.
conventions.shoulderFlexion: upper arm raised forward relative to the trunk (0 at sides, 180 overhead)
conventions.shoulderAbduction: upper arm raised sideways in the frontal plane
conventions.shoulderHorizontalAbduction: upper arm angle from the frontal plane, positive = elbows behind torso; null when not meaningful
conventions.hipAbduction: optional per-keyframe or exercise-level (hipAbductionDeg) thigh abduction from midline per side
conventions.asymmetric: when asymmetric=true, leg joint values are objects {left, right}; leadLeg names the working/lead leg. Mirror sides on alternate reps where noted.
conventions.widths: stanceWidthSW / gripWidthSW are multiples of shoulder (biacromial) width; stance measured between heel centres, grip between hands
conventions.keyframes: t in [0,1] over one rep; t spacing follows the tempo; first and last frames are the same pose. Interpolate with ease-in-out per segment.
conventions.tempo: seconds; order says which phase comes first; pauseAt says where the pause sits
conventions.consistency: For floor-standing frames with feet flat, trunkFromVertical = ankleDorsiflexion - kneeFlexion + hipFlexion (sagittal approximation). Wide stances (sumo, low bar) add hip abduction/external rotation, so drive the pelvis from trunkFromVertical and solve legs with IK to the fixed foot contacts.
conventions.ik: ikLimbs lists limbs whose end effector is pinned by fixedContacts and should be solved with 2-bone IK; other limbs use FK from the joint angles.

meta.unverifiedNote: Values marked angleBasis 'coaching_estimate' are standard coaching ranges chosen by the author for animation, not taken from a measured study. Shoulder width (SW) multiples derived from centimetre values assume biacromial width ~40 cm (an assumption).

sources.cite: Glassbrook DJ, et al. The high-bar and low-bar back-squats: a biomechanical analysis. J Strength Cond Res 2019;33(Suppl 1):S1-S18 (accepted manuscript, AUT repository).
sources.used: Table 4 sagittal peak-flexion 'actual' (interior) angles at 74-83% 1RM. Olympic weightlifters, high bar: hip 69+-7, knee 54+-7, ankle ROM 33+-4. Powerlifters, low bar: hip 59+-9, knee 62+-11, ankle ROM 33+-6. Hip = anterior angle thorax-to-thigh (acromion, greater trochanter, lateral epicondyle markers). Converted here as flexion = 180 - interior angle; ankleDorsiflexion taken as the ankle ROM. Lifters wore heeled weightlifting shoes.

sources.cite: Glassbrook DJ, et al. A review of the biomechanical differences between the high-bar and low-bar back-squat. J Strength Cond Res 2017;31(9):2618-2634.
sources.used: Qualitative: high bar = more knee flexion, less hip flexion, more upright torso; low bar = more forward lean, greater erector spinae, adductor and gluteal activity; high bar = greater quadriceps activity.

sources.cite: Escamilla RF, et al. A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2000;32(7):1265-1275.
sources.used: Abstract (read via Duke Scholars record): stance 70+-11 cm sumo vs 32+-8 cm conventional; foot turnout 42+-8 vs 14+-6 deg; grip 47+-4 vs 55+-10 cm; at liftoff and knee passage sumo trunk 5-10 deg more vertical, thigh 11-16 deg more horizontal; conventional knees and hips ~12 deg more extended. A secondary summary (not the primary paper) gives knee interior angle at knee passage of ~158-159 deg (about 21-22 deg flexion) for both styles: treated as unverified.

sources.cite: Gullett JC, et al. A biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals. J Strength Cond Res 2009;23(1):284-292.
sources.used: Qualitative: back squat produced higher knee compressive forces and knee extensor moments than front squat; muscle activity similar.

sources.cite: Yavuz HU, et al. Kinematic and EMG activities during front and back squat variations in maximum loads. J Sports Sci 2015.
sources.used: Qualitative: back squat showed significantly greater trunk lean than front squat with no knee kinematic differences. Exact degree values were not retrieved.

sources.cite: Brazil A, et al. A comprehensive biomechanical analysis of the barbell hip thrust. PLoS One 2021.
sources.used: 70% 1RM, 19 trained men: ROM hip 75+-19 deg, knee 21+-7 deg, pelvic-trunk 12+-21 deg; knee ~108+-8 deg and hip ~83+-16 deg flexed at peak hip extensor moment (early in the lift); mean lift time 0.83 s. Start/top absolute angles not reported.

sources.cite: Sconce E, et al. Agreement between methods and terminology used to assess the kinematics of the Nordic hamstring exercise. J Sports Sci 2021.
sources.used: Break-point angle 121.5+-10.4 deg and break-torque angle 126.0+-9.8 deg (as reported in search abstract). Read here as interior knee angle, i.e. roughly 54-60 deg knee flexion: the convention is our interpretation, not confirmed from the full text.

exercises.name: High-bar back squat
exercises.implementPlacement: back rack, high: bar on upper trapezius just below C7, above the spine of the scapula

keyframes.label: standing, braced
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, thumbs around bar, wrists stacked over elbows
keyframes.implementPosition: on upper traps, vertically over midfoot, at shoulder height

keyframes.label: standing, braced
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, thumbs around bar, wrists stacked over elbows
keyframes.implementPosition: on upper traps, vertically over midfoot, at shoulder height

cues: Big breath and brace before each descent
Knees travel forward and out over the toes
Sit straight down between the heels with chest up
Drive up keeping the bar over midfoot
mistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus) on the way up
Heels lifting or weight drifting to the toes
Hips shooting up first so the squat turns into a good morning
exercises.angleNotes: Bottom knee (126) and ankle (33) from S1 Olympic-weightlifter means. S1's hip (interior 69 -> flexion 111) gives trunk 18 deg, which in a 2D balance check puts the bar ~13 cm behind midfoot in flat shoes (S1 lifters wore heeled shoes), so hip flexion was raised to 127 (interior 53) to keep bar and system centre of mass over midfoot; trunk = ankle - knee + hip = 34. Intermediate frames are coaching estimates balanced the same way.

exercises.name: Low-bar back squat
exercises.implementPlacement: back rack, low: bar across rear delts on or just below the spine of the scapula

keyframes.label: standing, braced
keyframes.wristNotes: wrists straight in line with forearm, thumb over or beside bar; bar weight on back not hands

keyframes.label: standing, braced
keyframes.wristNotes: wrists straight in line with forearm

cues: Squeeze the bar into the back with elbows pulled back
Hips back and knees out at the same time
Keep the chest angle constant, do not let it collapse
Drive the upper back into the bar out of the hole
mistakes: Elbows flaring up so the bar rolls and loads the wrists
Chest dropping out of the bottom (good-morning squat)
Cutting depth above parallel
exercises.angleNotes: Bottom knee (118) and ankle (33) from S1 powerlifter means; hip 126 (interior 54) is within one SD of S1's 59+-9 and was chosen so the bar stays over midfoot (S1 mean hip gives trunk 36 and bar ~4 cm behind midfoot). Trunk = ankle - knee + hip. Intermediate frames are coaching estimates balanced in a 2D model.

exercises.name: Front squat
exercises.implementPlacement: front rack: bar on anterior delts against the throat, fingertips under bar, elbows high
cues: Elbows up, upper arms parallel to the floor
Sit straight down, torso tall
Knees forward and out
Lead out of the bottom with the elbows
mistakes: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
Bar weight carried in the hands instead of on the shoulders
Heels lifting from limited ankle dorsiflexion
exercises.angleNotes: S4/S5 support a more upright trunk than the back squat with similar knee motion; exact degrees are coaching estimates. shoulderFlexion is set to 90 + trunk lean so the upper arm stays horizontal.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: one dumbbell held vertically against the sternum, palms cupping the top head

keyframes.label: standing
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, palms up under the top plate

cues: Hold the weight tight to the chest
Sit between the heels, elbows inside the knees
Chest proud, spine long
Push the floor away
mistakes: Letting the dumbbell drift away from the chest
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Knees collapsing inward

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.implementPlacement: feet: 45-degree sled; feet mid-platform, back and hips on the reclined seat

keyframes.label: legs extended, soft knees
keyframes.bodyPlane: seated reclined; backrest angle machine-dependent; sled travels on a 45 deg rail

keyframes.label: bottom
keyframes.implementPosition: sled lowest point, thighs toward chest

cues: Keep hips and lower back pinned to the seat
Lower until just before the pelvis starts to tuck
Press through the whole foot
Stop just short of locking the knees
mistakes: Pelvis rolling off the seat at the bottom
Locking the knees hard at the top
Heels lifting off the platform
exercises.angleNotes: Leg angles relative to the machine; ankleDorsiflexion is shin relative to the footplate. Hips are fixed to the seat, so with a fixed footplate ankle change = knee change - hip change; values solved so the feet travel on a straight 45 deg rail for an assumed backrest reclined ~60 deg from vertical (machine-dependent assumption). Feet are IK targets on the moving sled.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.implementPlacement: shoulders under the machine pads, back flat on the sled pad, feet on the angled platform

keyframes.label: top, soft knees
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, hands on handles at the shoulder pads
keyframes.implementPosition: sled at top; trunk reclined on pad (machine-dependent ~45 deg)

cues: Keep the whole back flat on the pad
Knees travel forward over the toes
Full depth under control
Drive through the mid-foot
mistakes: Hips peeling off the pad at the bottom
Heels rising
Bouncing off the bottom
exercises.angleNotes: trunkFromVertical is negative (reclined back against the pad); the exact recline depends on the machine. ankleDorsiflexion is relative to the footplate. Values solved so the hip moves straight along the rail (assumed parallel to the back pad) while the feet stay fixed: top hip 25 reflects feet placed forward of the body line.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: dumbbells hanging at the sides
exercises.stanceNotes: Front ankle ~0.65 m (about 0.37 x height) ahead of the rear ankle; bench about 40-45 cm (just below knee height); rear laces on the bench with the foot pointing back and slightly down, rear ankle ~0.5 m above the floor. These distances are model assumptions for a 1.75 m lifter.
cues: Most of the weight on the front foot
Drop the back knee straight down
Slight forward lean, spine long
Drive through the front heel and mid-foot
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench so the heel lifts
Pushing off the rear foot
Front knee caving inward
exercises.angleNotes: Asymmetric: per-side values {left,right}; lead leg right. Rear (left) leg solved by IK so the rear ankle stays fixed on the bench in every frame. Rear ankle negative = plantarflexed; it is pointed hard at the top (about -59, near the end of range, ankle plus midfoot) and nearly neutral at the bottom where the shin is steep. Rear knee ends ~15 cm above the floor.

exercises.name: Walking lunge
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: dumbbells hanging at the sides
exercises.stanceNotes: One rep = one step: the root translates forward by one stride and the lead leg alternates each rep (mirror left/right on odd reps). The t=1 pose equals t=0 translated forward and mirrored.

keyframes.label: standing on lead leg, rear foot brought through
keyframes.implementPosition: dumbbells beside hips, one stride ahead

cues: Long enough step that the front shin stays near vertical
Drop the back knee toward the floor
Torso tall
Drive through the front foot to step through
mistakes: Short steps that push the front knee far over the toes and lift the heel
Feet on a tightrope line causing wobble
Leaning the torso far forward
exercises.angleNotes: At the bottom the rear foot is on the ball (toes extended, foot pitched ~75 deg) with the rear shin nearly horizontal, so the rear ankle reads as slight dorsiflexion (+15): ankle angle is shin relative to foot, not heel height. The rear ball of the foot stays on the same floor point from t=0.4 to t=0.6 and the front heel lands ~0.70 m ahead of it.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: dumbbells hanging at the sides
exercises.stanceNotes: Box about 45 cm (just below knee height for a 1.75 m lifter, model assumption); whole lead foot on the box; trail foot starts ~35 cm behind the lead ankle.

keyframes.label: standing tall on box
keyframes.implementPosition: dumbbells beside hips, raised by box height

keyframes.label: controlled lowering, trail toe reaching floor

cues: Drive through the whole foot on the box
Lean slightly forward to start
Do not push off the trail leg
Lower slowly under control
mistakes: Bouncing off the floor with the trail leg
Lead knee caving inward
Dropping down fast on the eccentric
exercises.angleNotes: Both start feet are flat (trunk = ankle - knee + hip on each side). At t=0.71 the trail toe just touches the floor one box-height below the lead foot.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: double-overhand grip, bar against the thighs

keyframes.label: hips back, bar above knees
keyframes.implementPosition: just above the knees, touching the thighs, over midfoot

keyframes.label: bottom, bar below the knees (upper shin)
keyframes.implementPosition: upper-to-mid shin, touching the legs, over midfoot

cues: Push the hips back, knees soft and fixed
Keep the bar dragging along the legs
Neutral spine, lats tight
Stop when the hips stop moving back
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower
Bending the knees into a squat
Bar drifting away from the legs
exercises.angleNotes: Bottom depth depends on hamstring flexibility. Shoulders sit ahead of the bar with the arms angled back (lats pulling the bar in), so shoulderFlexion = trunk - ~10-16 deg, not equal to trunk. Hips travel back behind the heels and shins tilt slightly back to keep bar and centre of mass over midfoot; this needs ~30 deg of knee bend at the bottom.

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: grip just outside the shins (double overhand, mixed or hook)

keyframes.label: setup / liftoff
keyframes.implementPosition: on floor, over midfoot, touching shins

tempo.notes: brief dead-stop reset on the floor between reps

cues: Bar over midfoot, shins touch the bar
Pull the slack out and brace before the floor breaks
Push the floor away, then hips through
Keep the bar close the whole way
mistakes: Hips shooting up first so the back rounds
Bar drifting forward away from the shins
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout
exercises.angleNotes: Stance (32 cm), turnout (14 deg) and grip (55 cm) from S3. Start and knee-passage angles are coaching estimates solved so straight arms (shoulders ~6-12 deg ahead of the bar) reach a 0.225 m bar centre touching the shins over midfoot; trunk = ankle - knee + hip. A secondary summary of S3 gives ~22 deg knee flexion at knee passage (unverified); the model needs ~27.

exercises.name: Sumo deadlift
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: grip inside the knees, arms vertical

keyframes.label: setup / liftoff
keyframes.implementPosition: on floor, over midfoot, close to shins

tempo.notes: brief dead-stop reset on the floor between reps

cues: Shins near vertical, knees pushed out over the toes
Chest up, hips close to the bar
Spread the floor apart as you push
Hips through at the top
mistakes: Knees caving in off the floor
Hips rising first so it becomes a stiff-legged pull
Stance so wide the knees track inside the feet
exercises.angleNotes: Stance (70 cm), turnout (42 deg), grip (47 cm) and 'trunk 5-10 deg more vertical than conventional' from S3. Sagittal hip/knee angles are projections; apply hipAbductionDeg and external rotation so knees track over the turned-out feet.

exercises.name: Good morning
exercises.implementPlacement: back rack, high: bar on upper trapezius

keyframes.label: hinging
keyframes.implementPosition: upper traps, ahead of midfoot while hips move back

keyframes.label: bottom, torso ~20 deg above parallel
keyframes.implementPosition: upper traps, ~15 cm ahead of midfoot; hips ~30 cm behind the ankles keep the combined centre of mass over midfoot

cues: Soft knees, then push the hips straight back
Keep the bar pinned to the upper back
Neutral spine throughout
Lead the return with the hips
mistakes: Rounding the upper or lower back
Going deeper than hamstring flexibility allows
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees
exercises.angleNotes: Balance solved for a bar of ~0.3-0.5 x bodyweight: the hips must travel well behind the heels with shins slightly back, which needs 20-30 deg of knee bend at depth.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
exercises.implementPlacement: hip crease (padded), held with both hands

keyframes.label: bottom, hips low
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, hands on bar over hips

cues: Chin tucked, ribs down
Drive through the heels
Shins vertical at the top
Squeeze the glutes, no lower-back arch
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of extending the hips
Feet too far out so hamstrings take over
Bench contact too high on the neck
exercises.angleNotes: Solved with the feet fixed and the upper back pivoting on a bench edge ~42 cm high: top = trunk and thighs horizontal, shins vertical (knee 90); bottom = trunk ~35 deg up from horizontal, hips ~20 cm off the floor, giving hip ROM 75 and knee ROM 20, matching S6 (75+-19, 21+-7). At the bottom the knees sit behind the ankles, so the ankle is plantarflexed (negative). Absolute angles are model estimates.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.implementPlacement: shin pad on the lower shin just above the ankle; knee aligned with machine pivot
cues: Line the knee up with the machine pivot
Hips down, hold the handles
Squeeze at the top
Control the lowering
mistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum
Hips lifting off the seat
Cutting the range short at the bottom

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
exercises.implementPlacement: ankle pad on the back of the lower calves just above the heels; knees just off the bench end

keyframes.label: legs extended
keyframes.bodyPlane: prone on bench, hips flexed ~20 deg by the angled bench (machine-dependent)

cues: Hips pressed into the pad
Curl heels toward glutes
Pause at the top
Lower slowly to almost straight
mistakes: Hips lifting off the bench
Jerking the weight up
Short, partial range

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.implementPlacement: thigh pad on top of the thighs above the knees; ankle pad behind the lower calves

keyframes.label: legs extended
keyframes.bodyPlane: seated upright, slight forward lean allowed

cues: Knees aligned with the pivot
Thigh pad locked down tight
Pull heels under the seat
Slow return to full stretch
mistakes: Thigh pad loose so hips slide
Using momentum
Not reaching full extension

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl
exercises.implementPlacement: none: ankles anchored under a pad or by a partner

keyframes.label: tall kneel
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, hands in front of chest

tempo.notes: concentric is a hand push-off back to kneeling

cues: Straight line from knees to head
Squeeze glutes so the hips stay extended
Lower as slowly as possible
Catch with the hands and push back up
mistakes: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever
Dropping fast early in the range
Arching the lower back
exercises.angleNotes: Body is one rigid line pivoting at the knee, so trunkFromVertical = 90 - kneeFlexion while hipFlexion ~0. Break point ~58 deg knee flexion interpreted from S7 (break-point angle ~121.5 deg); convention unconfirmed. Ankles plantarflexed under the anchor.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.implementPlacement: shoulders under the machine pads; balls of feet on the block edge
cues: Knees straight but not locked
Pause in the deep stretch
Rise onto the big toe
No bouncing
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom
Bending the knees to help
Partial range
exercises.angleNotes: ankleDorsiflexion negative = plantarflexion.

exercises.name: Seated calf raise
exercises.implementPlacement: knee pad on the distal thighs just above the knees; balls of feet on the block
cues: Knees at 90 degrees under the pad
Deep stretch at the bottom
Drive up through the big toe
Control every inch
mistakes: Bouncing
Rolling onto the outer edge of the foot
Partial range

exercises.name: Machine hip adduction
exercises.implementPlacement: pads on the inner thighs just above the knees
cues: Sit tall, back on the pad
Squeeze knees together
Pause at the close
Open slowly to a comfortable stretch
mistakes: Letting the weight stack slam
Rocking the torso forward
Starting wider than flexibility allows
exercises.angleNotes: hipAbduction (per side, deg from midline) is the moving joint; start width is machine/user set.

exercises.name: 45-degree back extension
exercises.implementPlacement: none (optional plate hugged to chest); hip pad just below the hip crease

tempo.notes: pause is a squeeze at the top

cues: Pad below the hip crease so the hips can hinge
Hinge at the hips, spine neutral
Squeeze glutes to rise
Stop in a straight line
mistakes: Hyperextending past a straight line at the top
Pad too high, blocking the hinge
Dropping fast into the bottom
exercises.angleNotes: Legs are fixed at ~45 deg forward lean on the bench, so trunkFromVertical = 45 + hipFlexion (can exceed 90: head below hips).

exercises.name: Front plank
exercises.implementPlacement: none

keyframes.label: hold
keyframes.bodyPlane: prone, elbows under shoulders, body straight ~10 deg above horizontal (head end higher)
keyframes.wristNotes: forearms flat, hands loose or lightly clasped

cues: Elbows under shoulders
Squeeze glutes and quads
Ribs down, slight posterior pelvic tilt
Breathe behind the brace
mistakes: Hips sagging into lumbar extension
Hips piked high
Head dropped or craned up

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
exercises.implementPlacement: hands on a pull-up bar, overhand grip
cues: Shoulders active, no dead swing
Curl the pelvis up, not just lift the legs
Pause at the top
Lower slowly without swinging
mistakes: Swinging for momentum
Only flexing the hips with an arched lower back
Dropping the legs fast
exercises.angleNotes: Hands fixed on the bar: as the trunk tilts back, shoulderFlexion = 180 + trunkFromVertical keeps the arms vertical. spineFlexion = posterior pelvic tilt/lumbar flexion; when present, hipFlexion is thigh relative to pelvis.

exercises.name: Kneeling cable crunch
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: rope from a high pulley, rope ends held beside the head

keyframes.label: start, kneeling tall-ish
keyframes.wristNotes: neutral, rope ends at the ears/forehead

keyframes.label: full crunch
keyframes.implementPosition: rope beside head, moved down toward knees

tempo.notes: pause is the squeeze in full flexion

cues: Lock the hips in place, do not sit back
Curl the ribs toward the pelvis
Keep the hands fixed beside the head
Control the stretch on the way up
mistakes: Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine
Pulling with the arms
Sitting back onto the heels
exercises.angleNotes: Thighs stay vertical; trunkFromVertical ~ hipFlexion + spineFlexion/2 (chord of a uniformly curved spine). Arms are fixed relative to the head.

exercises.name: Ab wheel rollout
exercises.implementPlacement: hands on the ab wheel handles; wheel rolls on the floor
cues: Hollow body: ribs down, glutes squeezed
Roll out only as far as you can keep the back from sagging
Arms straight
Pull back with the abs and lats
mistakes: Lower back sagging into an arch
Leading the return with the hips
Bending the elbows
exercises.angleNotes: Shins stay on the floor so thigh lean = 90 - kneeFlexion; trunkFromVertical ~ thigh lean + hipFlexion + spineFlexion/2. Wheel is an IK target sliding forward on the floor.

exercises.name: Power clean
exercises.implementPlacement: hands (hook grip) from floor -> front rack on anterior delts

keyframes.label: start (floor)
keyframes.wristNotes: hook grip, wrists slightly flexed, arms straight
keyframes.implementPosition: on floor over midfoot, touching shins

keyframes.label: bar passing knees (end of first pull)
keyframes.implementPosition: at knee height, close to legs

keyframes.label: full extension (triple extension)
keyframes.implementPosition: at upper thigh/hip crease, moving up fast

keyframes.label: catch (power position)
keyframes.implementPosition: front rack on delts, over midfoot

exercises.transitionNotes: Concentric (pull + catch) spans t 0-0.29 (1 s). The 1 s pause spans t 0.29-0.57: rise from the catch to a full front-rack stand by ~t 0.43 and hold. Eccentric 1.5 s spans t 0.57-1.0: drop the bar to the hang (~t 0.7) and hinge it to the floor. Renderers may insert an implicit standing-front-rack pose at t~0.43-0.57 and a hang pose at t~0.7.

tempo.notes: concentric ~1 s explosive pull and catch; pause = stand in front rack; eccentric = controlled return to floor

cues: Shoulders over the bar, push the floor away
Keep the bar close and sweep it into the hips
Jump and shrug, then pull under
Fast elbows to the front rack
mistakes: Bending the arms early
Bar looping away from the body
Catching with low elbows or a reverse-curl
exercises.angleNotes: Trunk angle held roughly constant through the first pull (55 -> 50), consistent with ISB/ISBS kinematic reports seen in search results (exact degrees not retrieved). Start solved so straight arms reach a 0.225 m bar centre over midfoot; knee passage has the bar just in front of the knees. At full extension the lifter is on the toes, so the floor-contact trunk formula does not apply.

exercises.name: Farmer's walk
exercises.implementPlacement: hands: heavy dumbbells or farmer's handles at the sides
exercises.stanceNotes: One cycle = two steps; root translates forward by two step lengths. Steps are short and quick under load.

tempo.notes: continuous walking; ~1.0-1.2 s per two-step cycle (coaching estimate); carry for distance or time

cues: Stand tall, shoulders down and back
Crush the handles
Short, quick steps
Brace and breathe shallow behind it
mistakes: Leaning forward or to one side
Long overstriding steps
Letting the shoulders roll forward
exercises.angleNotes: Leg angles are approximate normal-gait values, reduced for shorter loaded steps; general gait knowledge, not checked against a fetched source in this session.

changes: method: every keyframe re-checked with a 2D sagittal stick model (segment lengths as fractions of height after Winter's anthropometric table, applied from memory: shank 0.246H, thigh 0.245H, hip-to-acromion 0.288H, shoulder-to-grip 0.392H, ankle height 0.039H, midfoot ~0.035H ahead of the ankle; H = 1.75 m). Checks: trunk identity for flat-foot frames, bar / system centre of mass over midfoot (bar load 0.3-1.5 x bodyweight by lift), hands reaching a 0.225 m bar centre at floor pulls, fixed contacts reachable with constant positions across frames, machine rail constraints, tempo vs t spacing. All corrected values are model-derived coaching estimates, not measurements.

back_squat: mid-descent hip 78->92, trunk 23->37; bottom hip 111->127, trunk 18->34; mid-ascent hip 85->96, trunk 27->38. Old values put the bar 10-13 cm behind midfoot (lifter would fall backward in flat shoes); S1 hip kept only as a reference in angleNotes; angleBasis now measured+coaching_estimate.

low_bar_squat: mid-descent knee 62->65, ankle 14->16, hip 78->94, trunk 30->45; bottom hip 121->126, trunk 36->41; mid-ascent hip 97->106, trunk 40->49. Mid-descent had the bar ~11 cm behind midfoot; bottom now within S1's SD and balanced.

front_squat: mid-descent ankle 22->24, hip 63->75, trunk 10->24; bottom hip 102->117, trunk 12->27; mid-ascent ankle 25->26, hip 72->83, trunk 15->27; shoulderFlexion kept at 90 + trunk (114/117/117). Old trunk 10-15 deg put bar and centre of mass 10-12 cm behind midfoot; new trunk stays clearly more upright than the back squat (S4/S5).
